summary: Wrote src\en\module_04\12-concepts-c.md: concept sections s9 (1,053 words, target 950), s10 (1,349 / 1,250), s11 (1,211 / 1,200), s12 (849 / 850) and s13 (1,604 / 1,450), 6,066 words in all against 5,700 (+6%, every section within 15%), then 'What goes wrong' {#wrong} with all 14 slice items as symptom, cause and fix under ### headings (about 1,000 words). Every must_cover item is covered. All 13 planned worked examples are ::: worked boxes with step-by-step arithmetic, plus one small extra calculation in s9: 165 false alarms per true fault, a precision of 0.6%. All 8 figures (fig-04-14 to fig-04-21) are placed with precise captions, the ssm-kernel-explorer widget is in s13, and all 9 planned checks are ::: check / ::: answer pairs. Each section has one keyidea, except s9, s11 and s12; s11 has a pitfall on attention as explanation. All worked-example numbers were recomputed by script and match the plan: Gaussian tails, beam search, additive and dot attention, state against KV cache, TCN receptive field, the scalar recurrence and convolution, the complex mode, zero-order hold, LRU half-lives, FFT operation counts. The final check.mjs run (--module 4 --lang en --words) shows 0 errors. The warnings left are for parts other writers have not finished: labs, exercises, figure SVGs and widget JS.
changes: s10: the plan credits the finding that encoder-decoder quality falls with sentence length to 'Cho et al. 2014'. That observation is in Cho, van Merrienboer, Bahdanau and Bengio (2014), 'On the properties of neural machine translation: encoder-decoder approaches' (SSST-8 workshop), not the EMNLP GRU paper in the module's reference list. The text names the four authors so the two papers are not confused.

s10: the source says teacher forcing 'makes training parallel over positions'. The text corrects this as the plan intends: teacher forcing removes the sampling loop; only a transformer decoder then runs in parallel, and an RNN decoder still loops.

s11: the plan gives the per-step cost of additive attention as O(S d_a). The text gives O(S(d_a + H)), which also counts the weighted sum of the 2H-wide annotations. That is the same order when d_a is about H, and the O(S T') total is unchanged.

s9: the CUSUM is written for a change in residual variance, S_t = max(0, S_{t-1} + r_t^2/sigma^2 - kappa) with kappa a little above 1, because that is the fault type it is matched to. The plan names the CUSUM (Page 1954) but gives no form.

s13: the source said S4/Mamba 'train in parallel through a clever reformulation'. The text makes this precise: convolution mode for time-invariant models, and a parallel scan, derived from the associative composition of affine maps, when coefficients change with t (Mamba).
No numerical errors were found in the plan: every worked-example number in the slice was recomputed and matches.
issues: The module's reference list needs an entry: Cho, K., van Merrienboer, B., Bahdanau, D., Bengio, Y. 'On the properties of neural machine translation: encoder-decoder approaches.' SSST-8 Workshop, 2014. s10 cites it.

Inline maths split across two lines failed KaTeX when the second line started with '+', which Markdown reads as a list bullet. Every split inline expression in this file was joined onto one line, so a few prose lines exceed 100 characters. Other parts (for example 11-concepts-b.md) also split inline maths across lines and could hit the same failure if a continuation line starts with '+', '-' or a number followed by '.'.
Links to #lab1-#lab5 and #e15 resolve only once the labs and exercises parts are written.

s9 and s13 sit at +11% of target, and the Lab 3 and Lab 4 numbers quoted in s9-s11 are the plan's expected values. If the execution phase changes them, update the prose: s9's monitor delays and false-alarm counts, s10's 79%/59% and 100/62/2%, s11's alignment argmaxes and peak weights, and s13's Lab 5 timings and recall results.
s12 quotes the comparison table's compute-per-layer row from Vaswani et al. (2017) as an added row. The row is standard, but the figure caption for fig-04-19 lists only the four rows the plan names.
